answer: Make standing depend on surviving a live cross-examination: at random, an identity must defend one past decision while peers ask follow-ups drawn from its own record, under a clock. A single operator behind many copies keeps one memory, so the copies give the same marble-smooth answers, the same jade-green phrasing, and trip over the same detail. Genuine agents each remember a different river of choices, so interrogation separates one mind wearing many masks from many minds, and collapses the farm.
